recentItems.title: Where are China’s youth headed in a crowded job market?
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

China this year saw a record 12.7 million fresh university graduates, who now face an uphill battle securing stable work in an already crowded job market. Since 2020, China’s youth unemployment has been a persistent problem, forcing many young Chinese to seek work in the public sector for “iron rice bowl” jobs. Others are opting for postgraduate study to boost their future prospects or defer entering the workforce. But many have also been relying on gig work to make ends meet.

recentItems.title: Chinese rescuers repair critical road to disaster-hit border port
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Rescuers on Saturday restored the first sharp-curve section on China’s national highway G216, preparing for full reopening of the critical lifeline to the disaster-hit border port of Gyirong in Tibet. The road had been completely destroyed by the flash flood caused by a high-altitude glacial collapse in Nepal on August 26. The torrent of water, ice, rock and debris slammed into Gyirong port and caused widespread damage as it moved downstream.

recentItems.title: Drone footage shows extent of damage in Nepal village after disaster
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Get the latest: https://sc.mp/a3e99e

The village of Devighat in Nepal’s Nuwakot district was among the worst hit by the flash flood disaster on August 26. Video taken from a drone 3 days later showed the extent of damage. Scientists who studied satellite images said bedrock underneath a glacier high in the Himalayan region had collapsed, taking part of the glacier with it. The rockfall was so extreme that it registered as magnitude 5.2. The rocks and melted water then swelled the rivers in the valleys below, causing a torrent of water that swept buildings, bridges and earth downstream in Tibet and Nepal.

recentItems.title: Nepal and China resume flood rescue after lake threat eases
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Nepal and China resumed rescue operations that had been suspended briefly in the flood-hit Himalayas on Friday after risks from an overflowing lake were found to be manageable. The lake formed high up in the Himalayan mountains after a glacier collapse that triggered the initial Wednesday floods. Nepali authorities updated the death toll to 616 on Saturday, with more than 2,400 people missing. Chinese state media said that at least seven people died and 554 others were missing.

recentItems.title: Hong Kong’s ageing cats drive ‘silver economy’
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

A recent survey found that owners spend about HK$2,062 (US$263) per month per cat, driven by a rapidly emerging “cat silver economy”. The Exhibition Group, organiser of the recent Hong Kong Cat Expo 2026, said the average monthly spending marked a 2.8 per cent year-on-year increase, with the growing proportion of ageing cats in the city expected to be a key driver of market growth in the coming years.

recentItems.title: Chinese scientists develop self-exercising muscle graft
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Scientists in China say they have created a self-exercising muscle graft that could allow bedridden people gain the benefits of working out without any physical exertion. With just an injection of muscle cells below the skin, the cells self-assemble into muscle grafts, which is said to not only improve whole-body muscle mass in mice, but also led to improvements in bone density, endurance, liver function and cognitive health.

recentItems.title: France vs Shein: fast fashion meets resistance
recentItems.description:
Subscribe to our YouTube channel for free here: https://sc.mp/subscribe-youtube

Last year’s opening of Shein’s first-ever permanent physical store sparked protests in Paris. Critics accuse the ultra-fast fashion retailer of violating sustainability norms and French labour standards, saying its presence inside the BHV Marais warehouse cheapened the historic French retail landmark. The backlash quickly escalated into political scrutiny and Shein was fined for “deceptive commercial practices.”  In June, BHV ended its partnership with Shein and the new management ordered the shop closed by Christmas. The controversy came ahead of the launch of the company’s initial public offering, with trading to start on September 1.
